newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin has no news on Yeltsin before afternoon.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin has no news on Yeltsin before afternoon.

text.p: The Kremlin had no news to issue on President Boris Yeltsin's condition on Wednesday morning, a spokesman for the presidential press service said.
The next information on his health was expected at a briefing by chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov and Yeltsin's press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky at 2.30 p.m. (1130 GMT).
The presidential press service said in a statement on Tuesday evening: "His condition has improved considerably, he is more physically active."
"There is only sporadic wheeziness in his lungs," it said.

The president, who turns 66 on February 1, held his first official meeting on Tuesday since he fell ill. He had previously met only his doctors and family at the Central Clinical Hospital in Moscow where he was taken a week ago.
The presidential press service said those talks, with Krmelin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais, lasted 40 minutes and that they had discussed the general political situation and personnel matters.
The doctors' report on Tuesday appeared to point to the biggest improvement in Yeltsin's condition since he fell ill.
But there was still no indication when the president, who had heart surgery on November 5 and did not return to work in the Kremlin until December 23, would leave hospital.
